title: International Ayurveda Conference in Udupi to Tackle Autoimmune Disorders
excerpt: Kshamatvam 2026, the 6th international conference hosted by SDM College of Ayurveda, will bring together up to 2,000 delegates from multiple countries to explore translational Ayurvedic research on autoimmune diseases.
body:
• Kshamatvam 2026 runs September 29–October 1 at SDM College of Ayurveda in Udupi, Karnataka, with 1,500 to 2,000 delegates expected from India and abroad
  • The conference will feature speakers from Germany, Italy, and Argentina alongside Indian researchers, focusing on immune modulation and evidence-based Ayurvedic practices
  • Early bird registration is open until August 31; abstract submissions close August 30

Sri Dharmasthala Manjunatheshwara College of Ayurveda, Hospital & Research Centre in Udupi, Karnataka, will host Kshamatvam 2026 — the 6th International Conference on Translational Ayurveda in Autoimmune Disorders — from September 29 to October 1. The three-day event, themed "Bridging Classical Wisdom with Global Healthcare," is expected to draw between 1,500 and 2,000 delegates, according to conference organizers.

Conference Scope and Topics

Autoimmune diseases — conditions in which the body's immune system attacks healthy tissues, damaging organs, joints, skin, and the nervous system — are among the fastest-growing health challenges worldwide. The conference is framed as a response to that trend, with sessions on immune modulation, translational research, and evidence-based Ayurvedic practices.

Professor Prasanna N. Mogasale, the conference's organizing secretary and a faculty member in the Department of Roganidana at SDM College, has pointed to environmental and lifestyle shifts as potential triggers for autoimmune flare-ups. According to a report by Health and Family, Mogasale cited chronic stress, irregular sleep, highly processed diets, environmental pollution, and disrupted circadian rhythms as factors that may destabilize immune function in genetically susceptible individuals.

Ayurvedic concepts including Vyadhikshamatva (the body's natural disease resistance), Bala (constitutional strength), Ojas (vital essence), and Rasayana (rejuvenation therapies) will be discussed alongside contemporary immunological frameworks. The conference aims to examine where these traditional ideas intersect with — and can be tested against — modern clinical science.

International and Indian Faculty

The speaker roster spans multiple countries. International faculty includes Dr. Christian Kessler from Germany, Dr. Antonio Morandi from Italy, and Dr. Jorge Luis Berra from Argentina, according to the Annals of Ayurvedic Medicine. Indian speakers include Dr. Bhushan Patwardhan of Savitribai Phule Pune University, Dr. Sanjeev Rastogi, Dr. Rammanohar Puthiyedath, Dr. Yogesh Bendale, and Dr. Prashanth A.S., among others.

"While integration is desirable, it must be earned through transparent, rigorous experimentation and systematic documentation. Traditional systems cannot rely on the authority of classical texts alone; they must deliver measurable evidence regarding safety, quality, and clinical efficacy."

— Dr. Bhushan Patwardhan, Savitribai Phule Pune University, writing in the EPMA Journal

Current Evidence and Cautions

Clinical evidence for Ayurvedic interventions in autoimmune conditions remains uneven. According to a review published in the EPMA Journal, the field has historically been constrained by insufficient sample sizes, a lack of standardization in herbal formulations, and inadequate safety tracking. Controlled trials evaluating integrative approaches for knee osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis have shown encouraging signals, but researchers stress these do not prove broad effectiveness across all autoimmune conditions.

Product safety remains a concern. Peer-reviewed literature has documented instances of heavy metal contamination in unregulated Ayurvedic products. Health experts emphasize that any integrative approach must involve licensed clinicians, quality-tested formulations, and medical monitoring — particularly for patients on immunosuppressive drugs, corticosteroids, or biological agents.

Logistics and Registration

Pre-conference workshops on Tuesday, September 29, will precede the main sessions on September 30 and October 1 at the Bhavaprakasha Auditorium on SDM's Kuthpady campus. Padma Vibhushana Dr. D. Veerendra Heggade, Dharmadhikari of Sree Kshethra Dharmasthala and Chancellor of SDM University, serves as chief patron. Dr. Mamatha K.V., Principal of SDMCAH & RC, is the chief organizing secretary.

Early bird registration runs until August 31, 2026. Fees range from Rs. 2,500 plus GST for undergraduates to Rs. 3,500 plus GST for faculty and practitioners. International delegates pay $60 plus GST, with a reduced rate of $45 for delegates from BIMSTEC member countries. Meals and a conference kit are included; accommodation is not.

What's Next

Abstract submissions close August 30. Late registration at a 10% premium is available from September 1 through September 28, with spot registration at 20% above early-bird rates after that. The WHO's Global Traditional Medicine Strategy has continued to push for safety and evidence standards in traditional medicine systems globally — a backdrop that gives conferences like Kshamatvam added weight as the field seeks broader credibility.
